statement.p: Find the equation of the hyperboloid of one sheet passing through the points (\pm 3,0,0),(0,\pm 7,0) and (\pm 6,0,5),(0,\pm 14,5)

static.solution:
z=z_{0} are ellipses. Hence, the equation of the hyperboloid has the form
\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{y}{b}\right)^2-\left(\frac{z}{c}\right)^2=1
Substituting z=0 we get
\left(\frac{x}{a}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{y}{b}\right)^2=1
By the given information this ellipse has x and y intercepts at the points (\pm 3,0),(0,\pm 7). So we get
\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{y}{7}\right)^2-\left(\frac{z}{c}\right)^2=1
Substituting z=5 we get
\frac{x^2}{3^2} + \frac{y^2}{7^2} -\frac{5^2}{c^2}=1
\frac{x^2}{9} + \frac{y^2}{49} =1+\frac{25}{c^2}=\frac{c^2+25}{c^2}
\frac{c^2 x^2}{9(c^2+25)} + \frac{c^2 y^2}{49(c^2+25)} = 1
\left(\frac{x}{\frac{3}{c}\sqrt{c^2+25}}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{y}{\frac{7}{c}\sqrt{c^2+25}}\right)^2=1
By the given information the following must hold: \frac{3}{c}\sqrt{c^2+25}=6 and \frac{7}{c}\sqrt{c^2+25}=14
\frac{\sqrt{c^2+25}}{c}=2, so c^2+25=4c^2 and 3c^2=25
Thus, c=\frac{5}{\sqrt{3}}, and by substituting we obtain the following equation
\left(\frac{x}{3}\right)^2 +\left(\frac{y}{7}\right)^2-\left(\frac{z}{\frac{5}{\sqrt{3}}}\right)^2=1
